en: Well, let's give it our all today.
! How're you doing?
Morning, morning! Huh, you look sluggish.
Not a morning person, are you? Ahaha.
Good evening. Got a moment?
Your watch seems to have stopped.
Hm? ...Ah, so it has.
Still, how did you notice?
Ha! How could I not?
I'm Dean, the clockmaker.
In my line of work, these things catch my eye.
I see...
Bring that watch by my shop.
I'll have it fixed in no time.
Yes, I'll do that. Most helpful.
Anything about clocks, just ask me!
! Hi there.
Bring me that watch, will you?
Not knowing the time must be awkward, eh?
Whoa, just the fellow I wanted to see!
So, have you been keeping well?
<Well enough>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); stern branch of msg 66455. Leads to #1943-#1945.

en: <No, I can't say I am>
What, just 'well enough'?
Well, same here. The old clock shop man, see,
note: Ends with ',' : #1945 continues the sentence on the next line.

en: he's been a real nag lately. We always fight.
Oh dear, not enough sleep or something?
You do look a bit pale.
At your age, you have to mind your health.
Hello, welcome!
A repair? Or maybe a new clock?
Is this a clock shop?
No, it's a clock factory, but we sell too.
Better goods than that stubborn old man's,
and above all, my repairs are guaranteed.
Anyway, beware the old clock shop man.
He all but forces you to buy.
Oh, I've seen your face somewhere. Hello.
Ah, we met in the street! Good to see you.
Need a clock repaired?
I may be young, but Dean's work is reliable.
You can trust my skill.
Oh my, back again?
Hello, hello! Good to see you.
What brings you today? A repair?
Or shall I badmouth the old clock shop man?
Joking aside, though.
It's not as if I fall out with him
for no reason. We just see things differently.
I want to do good, honest work.
But that old man only cares about money.
That's rude to the customers, isn't it?
You quite like seeing the factory, huh?
Well, I'm not that busy myself, so that's fine.
Few young folks take up this kind of work.
I guess they want something flashier.
Me, I'm content with it,
note:
Msg 66649: #1976

#1977 / #1978

#1979, each piece continues the same sentence. #1977 and #1979 start with an explicit space (single use); auto_space would treat fun|and as a word split by the pause and add none.

en: I love this work,
so every day is fun
and rewarding too.
If only that idiot old man weren't around.
Hello, how are things?
Me, I'm so-so. Still, ordinary's best.
By the way, isn't that watch precious to you?
And here I am offering to fix it.
Don't be shy, it's on the house.
Yes, hello. Who is it?
A repair? Then come to the factory by day.
The factory's big, you can't miss it.
Come by tomorrow or later, then.
! Oh, hello.
Sorry, I'm in a foul mood today.
I clashed with the clock shop man over work.
Don't want to take it out on you. Later, okay?
You worried about me?
Don't worry, craftsmen are a stubborn lot.
Fights like that happen all the time.
Hello,
note: Before the name: Dean '{NAME}, welcome!' (#443) and Maurice '{NAME}.' (#98).

en: Coming in? Today's been my lucky day.
Got a clock order from a wealthy family.
